Combine the RankIndex terms into a priority score

Source: R/fn_rank.R
rank_index.Rd

Assembles \(\text{Rank}(x) = D_g + D_r + S + A + C\) from whichever terms you supply. Each term is a per-patch vector (patches in the same order); the result is a data.frame of the rescaled components plus the combined index and its rank.

Usage

rank_index(..., weights = NULL, rescale = TRUE)

Arguments

...

named per-patch term vectors, e.g. Dg = dg, Dr = dr, S = s, A = a, C = c; all equal length. A single named list or data.frame may be passed instead.

weights

optional named numeric of per-term multipliers; names must match the supplied terms, partial is fine (unlisted terms get 1).

rescale

min–max each term to \([0,1]\) first (default TRUE).

Value

a data.frame with one column per (rescaled) term, an index column (the weighted-mean priority on \([0,1]\)) and an integer rank (1 = highest priority); the weights used are on attribute weights.

Details

  • Rescaled. Every input is min–max rescaled to \([0,1]\) so terms on different native scales are comparable before combining. (The term functions already emit \([0,1]\) and are oriented high = higher priority; this only guarantees it.) Set rescale = FALSE to trust the inputs as-is.

  • Weighted. weights gives a per-term multiplier; unnamed terms default to 1 (all equal). The index is the weighted mean over the terms present for a patch, so it stays in \([0,1]\) and is comparable however many terms are included.

  • Skippable. Only the terms you pass are used — drop S (or any other) simply by not supplying it.

  • NA-safe. A patch missing one term is scored on its remaining terms (the weighted mean renormalises per row); a patch missing every term is NA.
